Use case: stylized-concept. Create a high quality landscape art-direction board for STILL WARM, an adult Victorian first-person horror game. This is a NEW DESIGN from scratch. Input image is ONLY a reference for the existing game's restricted palette, fine ordered pixel dithering and darkness. Do NOT copy its cartoon character, anatomy, geometric props, UI, composition, text, or badge.
Board layout: large left panel (about 70% width) is a convincing in-game first-person scene. Narrow right panel is a close-up study of the SAME creature's head and one hand, with realistic anatomy. Small clean title at top and 5 tiny palette swatches at bottom; no other text. No game HUD.
Left scene: view from the eyes of an injured adult man reclining in a wrecked Victorian laboratory, looking down along HIS OWN torso and limbs with a corpse helper beside him. His visible body must be anatomically credible: connected shoulders and upper arms, foreshortened ribcage tapering to a waist, pelvis and two legs continuing naturally away; ordinary-sized hands with five fingers relaxed on either side. Rumpled open work shirt, narrow exposed strip of bruised sternum, waist and legs covered by stained trousers/linen, a heavy broken ceiling timber pinning upper thighs. One small dark blood stain; no exposed organs. Include the patient's body prominently in lower half; do not show the patient's head or an external view of his body. The creature is visible above it, face readable. Old gas lamp, wood, iron, dirty linen. The room can be built with a few assets.
Style: adult survival-horror, lifelike human proportions and practical prosthetic creature makeup translated to low-resolution real-time 3D, then quantized through a fine six-color ordered dither screen. Harsh pockets of readable light in deep shadows. Fine visible pixel pattern, strong masses and silhouettes, not smooth cinematic photorealism and not painted brushwork. No giant jaw, no oversized nose/ears/head, no cute eyes, no heroic physique, no cartoon smile, no cel shading, no mascot, no obvious low-poly triangles or primitive spheres. Dread comes from a body that should be dead standing very still too close to you.
Direction A title: "A — THE EXHUMED"
Creature: an ordinary middle-aged adult man recently taken from a grave, human face at normal scale, slack uneven cheeks, deep-set unfocused small eyes, waxy grey pallor and subtle bruised discoloration, thin ragged lips barely parted, a modest uneven seam disappearing under his jaw. Short thinning dirty hair. Tall but normally proportioned, slightly stooped with narrow lowered shoulders and long natural hands. Faded black wool waistcoat over a dirty collarless work shirt with sleeves rolled to the elbows; practical late-Victorian mortuary clothing. He looks frightened and physically ruined, not angry or theatrical. No face wraps, mask, spectacles, neck bolts or obvious monster clichés.
Palette: near-black, charcoal, cold grey-green, aged bone, with a restrained dried oxblood accent. Gaslight rakes the side of the face and hands. Patient body has the warmest remaining skin tone. The intimate believable face and anatomy should be the clear focus.

Direction B title: "B — THE DROWNED"
Creature: a broad ordinary adult male corpse recovered from cold water, realistic soft dead weight and normal sized head, slightly swollen mottled grey skin, heavy eyelids over small unfocused eyes, wet sparse hair stuck to scalp, lax closed mouth, subtly asymmetrical sagging jaw; no gaping monster grin. Body of patient is clammy with taut normal anatomical wrists, blood smear caught in shirt wrinkles. Make the fear tactile: wet sleeves close to living skin. Avoid bright teal or glossy fantasy monster styling.
